originalTitle: Where gold price is headed next as Fed rate hike and inflation odds change direction
summary: Gold prices have been volatile in 2026, but a recent rally shows renewed investor interest amid tamer inflation data and changing Fed rate expectations.
content:
In 2026, gold has been a tough trade to time right, falling from a 10-year high over $5,300 an ounce that it reached early in the year by as much as 18%, according to Goldprice.org . But last week was the precious metal's best week since January, while gold mining stocks had their hottest five-day run since 2008. With volatility in the gold trade leaving it with a year-to-date return that is now close to flat, some are betting that the trading chart direction is going to continue up. But there are potential pitfalls ahead. After all, even with its recent dramatic moves , the price of gold is still higher by over $1,000 in the past one-year period.

"Gold is the new gold," said Pippa Malmgren, a former Special Assistant to President George W. Bush and member of the National Economic Council.

Malmgren says what has attracted investors to gold has not changed. Many are scared that fiscal spending is out of control in the U.S. and that growth will be weak everywhere else. "This implies inflation," Malmgren said. She added that the Trump administration's pursuit of expensive foreign wars , as well as its embrace of cryptocurrencies, both add to uneasiness among some investors.

"This makes nervous investors turn to conservative methods for preserving value, such as buying gold," Malmgren said. Central banks around the world, meanwhile, are expanding their gold holdings, which she says further signals a loss of confidence in fiat money, led by continued buying of gold by China.

"Central banks never stopped buying," said Patrick Kennedy, founder and managing partner of Hartford, Connecticut-based AllSource Investment Managementd. "The PBOC added 19.9 tons in July, its largest month since October 2023 and its 21st straight month of accumulation," Kennedy said.

That bullishness is shared by billionaire hedge fund manager John Paulson , who recently told CNBC that gold is only in early stages of a long-term rally, citing loss of faith in paper currency and runaway government spending (Paulson has been a gold bull since 2009).

While fear has been a driver of the gold rush mentality historically, Joe Cavatoni, senior market strategist at the World Gold Council, says he views the recent bounce among U.S. investors as more of an opportunistic trade.

"Gold's recent rebound appears to be driven more by changing expectations around interest rates and the economy than by fear alone," Cavatoni said. "There are signs of weakening, particularly on the jobs front, and markets are responding quickly. As investors adjust their outlook for rates, gold is reacting the way you'd expect a highly macro-sensitive asset to respond," Cavatoni said.

"My sense is that the U.S. flows driving this move are more tactical in nature, as we have seen GLD options activity increase , while the buying we're seeing out of Asia and Europe tends to be stickier," Cavatoni said, referring to flows into the SPDR Gold Shares ETF ( GLD ), with investors in both regions adding to their holdings.

With expectations for a rate hike from the Federal Reserve coming down after the latest inflation data was viewed by the market as tame, the appeal of gold versus other rate-sensitive assets and against a soft U.S. dollar typically increases.

"I wouldn't view gold simply as a safe-haven asset. Many investors are using it as a wealth preservation tool and to help diversify portfolios amid ongoing uncertainty about growth and policy," Cavatoni said.

Kennedy says that the recent flows into ETFs, which reached a six-week high, is professional money, not just retail chasing.

GLD was higher by roughly 1% on Wednesday.

Expectations for a rate hike were declining even before the latest inflation print, said Nick Cawley, a contributing analyst for Solomon Global, a UK-based gold and silver bullion dealer, down by over 20-percentage points in the past week.

"This suggests markets are growing more cautious about further U.S. rate increases," he said, pointing to the recent benign trend in the inflation data and last Friday's soft non-farm payrolls report.

Kennedy says his firm's view was that the first half selloff in gold was a buying opportunity rather than the sign of a top. "We bought and added to GLDM off the July technical bottom," he said, referring to another share class of GLD which has a lower expense ratio.

But he says declining expectations for a rate hike are not the same as a Fed positioned to cut. "This is not a rate cut trade, at least not yet. The Fed has been parked at 3.50 to 3.75 all year and September was genuinely live for a hike right up until the payrolls miss," Kennedy said.

"What changed is that the hike tail risk came out of the market," Kennedy said, noting this morning's CPI at 0.1 percent monthly and 3.4 percent annual, with core at 2.5 percent, was in line and keeps that narrative going. "It's a different setup than a cutting cycle, and it matters when you're asking whether this has legs," Kennedy added.

From a technical standpoint, last week's move above the 50-day moving average, along with the break of this year's pattern of lower highs, should support further gains, Cawley said, with any pullbacks expected to be short-lived and viewed as opportunities to re-enter gold's next leg higher.

Gold miners see increased investor interest

Some traders and investors have turned to the trade in gold mining stocks in a search for value within the equities market, said Vince Stanzione, an independent trade and author of "The Millionaire Dropout."

"Many quality mining stocks are trading on single digit forward P/Es and paying great dividends," Stanzione said, pointing to AngloGold Ashanti and S&P 500 member Newmont . He added that many retail traders prefer to use ETFs, with the most popular being Van Eck Gold Miners ( GDX ), which covers the larger mining stocks, and Van Eck Junior Gold Miners ( GDXJ ), which covers the junior miners.

chineseTitle: 随着美联储加息和通胀可能性改变方向，金价下一步走向
chineseSummary: 2026 年金价一直波动较大，但近期的反弹表明，在通胀数据温和和美联储利率预期发生变化的情况下，投资者的兴趣重新燃起。
chineseContent:
根据 Goldprice.org 的数据，2026 年黄金交易非常艰难，从年初触及的每盎司 5,300 美元以上的 10 年高点下跌了 18%。但上周是贵金属自 1 月份以来表现最好的一周，而金矿股则经历了自 2008 年以来最热的五日涨幅。由于黄金交易的波动导致其年初至今的回报率目前接近持平，一些人押注交易图表方向将继续上涨。但前方存在潜在的陷阱。毕竟，尽管金价近期出现大幅波动，但在过去一年内金价仍上涨了 1,000 美元以上。

“黄金是新的黄金，”乔治·W·布什总统前特别助理、国家经济委员会成员皮帕·马尔姆格伦说。

马尔姆格伦表示，吸引投资者投资黄金的因素并没有改变。许多人担心美国的财政支出失控，而其他地方的增长也将疲弱。 “这意味着通货膨胀，”马尔姆格伦说。她补充说，特朗普政府追求代价高昂的对外战争，以及对加密货币的拥抱，都增加了一些投资者的不安。

马尔姆格伦表示：“这使得紧张的投资者转向保守的保值方法，例如购买黄金。”与此同时，世界各国央行正在扩大黄金持有量，她表示，这进一步表明，在中国持续购买黄金的带动下，人们对法定货币失去了信心。

总部位于康涅狄格州哈特福德的 AllSource Investment Managementd 创始人兼执行合伙人帕特里克·肯尼迪 (Patrick Kennedy) 表示：“央行从未停止购买。”肯尼迪表示：“中国人民银行 7 月份增持了 19.9 吨，这是自 2023 年 10 月以来最大的月份，也是连续 21 个月增持。”

亿万富翁对冲基金经理约翰·保尔森 (John Paulson) 也持同样的乐观态度，他最近向 CNBC 表示，黄金仅处于长期上涨的早期阶段，理由是人们对纸币失去信心，政府支出失控（保尔森自 2009 年以来一直看好黄金）。

尽管从历史上看，恐惧一直是淘金热心态的驱动因素，但世界黄金协会高级市场策略师乔·卡瓦托尼(Joe Cavatoni)表示，他认为美国投资者近期的反弹更多是一种机会主义交易。

卡瓦托尼表示：“金价近期的反弹似乎更多是受到利率和经济预期变化的推动，而不仅仅是恐惧。”卡瓦托尼表示：“有疲软的迹象，特别是在就业方面，市场正在迅速做出反应。随着投资者调整利率前景，黄金的反应方式与你预期的对宏观高度敏感的资产的反应方式相同。”

卡瓦托尼表示：“我的感觉是，推动这一走势的美国资金流本质上更具战术性，因为我们看到 GLD 期权活动有所增加，而亚洲和欧洲的买盘往往更具粘性。”他指的是流入 SPDR 黄金股 ETF (GLD) 的资金，这两个地区的投资者都在增持。

由于市场认为最新通胀数据温和，美联储加息的预期下降，黄金相对于其他利率敏感资产以及相对疲软美元的吸引力通常会增加。

卡瓦托尼表示：“我不会仅仅将黄金视为避险资产。许多投资者将其用作财富保值工具，并在增长和政策持续不确定的情况下帮助实现投资组合多元化。”

肯尼迪表示，近期流入 ETF 的资金达到了六周以来的最高点，是专业资金，而不仅仅是散户追逐的资金。

周三 GLD 上涨约 1%。

英国金银交易商 Solomon Global 的特约分析师尼克·考利 (Nick Cawley) 表示，即使在最新的通胀数据公布之前，加息预期也在下降，过去一周下降了 20% 以上。

“这表明市场对美国进一步加息变得更加谨慎，”他表示，并指出近期通胀数据的良性趋势和上周五疲软的非农就业报告。

肯尼迪表示，他的公司认为上半年黄金的抛售是一个买入机会，而不是见顶的迹象。他表示：“我们在 7 月技术底部买入并增持了 GLDM。”他指的是 GLD 的另一类股票，其费用比率较低。

但他表示，加息预期下降并不等同于美联储准备降息。 “这不是降息交易，至少目前还不是。美联储全年都将利率维持在3.50至3.75之间，9月份确实是加息的日子，直到就业数据未达到预期，”肯尼迪表示。

肯尼迪表示：“变化在于，加息尾部风险已从市场中消失。”他指出，今天上午的消费者物价指数 (CPI) 月度上涨 0.1%，年率上涨 3.4%，核心上涨 2.5%，符合预期，并让这种说法继续下去。 “这是一种与切割循环不同的设置，当你问它是否有腿时，它很重要，”肯尼迪补充道。

考利表示，从技术角度来看，上周金价突破50日移动均线，加上今年低点模式的突破，应该会支撑金价进一步上涨，任何回调预计都将是短暂的，并被视为金价重新进入下一阶段走高的机会。

金矿商看到投资者兴趣增加

独立交易者、《百万富翁辍学》一书的作者文斯·斯坦齐奥内 (Vince Stanzione) 表示，一些交易员和投资者已转向金矿股交易，以在股票市场中寻找价值。

Stanzione 表示：“许多优质矿业股的远期市盈率为个位数，并支付丰厚的股息。”他指的是 AngloGold Ashanti 和标准普尔 500 指数成员 Newmont。他补充说，许多零售交易者更喜欢使用 ETF，其中最受欢迎的是涵盖较大矿业股的 Van Eck Gold Miners (GDX) 和涵盖初级矿业股的 Van Eck Junior Gold Miners (GDXJ)。
